name: SKIN
description: Skin (or 'Georgia Skin') is a legendary high-stakes gambling game from the American South. It is a banking game, but not in the traditional sense where the bank has an edge; the edge comes purely from chance, nerve, and 'side bets'. Cards are dealt from a shoe one by one. Players bet on their card being matched by a card from the deck. If your card is matched (falls), you lose. The last card standing ('The Skin') is the winner unless all bets are resolved earlier. It is famous for its slow, tension-filled reveal ('Skinning').

content.text: Skin (or 'Georgia Skin') is a legendary high-stakes gambling game from the American South. It is a banking game, but not in the traditional sense where the bank has an edge; the edge comes purely from chance, nerve, and 'side bets'. Cards are dealt from a shoe one by one. Players bet on their card being matched by a card from the deck. If your card is matched (falls), you lose. The last card standing ('The Skin') is the winner unless all bets are resolved earlier. It is famous for its slow, tension-filled reveal ('Skinning').
Developed in the 19th century among African American communities in the South, likely derived from Faro. It was notorious in juke joints and turpentine camps.

Two or more players; Scarne describes it as best for about six. One player is the banker (dealer). The first banker is chosen by dealing cards one at a time until an Ace appears; the turn to be banker passes to the right after each deal. Each player may accept one case card from the dealer to bet on, or refuse; the dealer also holds one card. Cards are revealed one by one from a dealing box or shoe.
Players buy a card from the dealer (the 'Case Card'). Dealer takes a card too.

items.text: Standard (Scarne): The form described by John Scarne in Scarne on Cards: single 52-card pack, dealing box, one case card per player, banker's card, fresh cards, side bets.
